topics.summary: A Wo? question is answered in the dative, usually with stehen, sitzen, liegen or hängen.

explanation.heading: The rule
explanation.text: When asking a Wo? question, the answer will be in the dative case.

explanation.heading: The four verbs
explanation.text: The answer often contains stehen, sitzen, liegen or hängen — verbs of position rather than of movement.

explanation.heading: Reading the arrows
explanation.text: The document writes the dative form and then the nominative it came from in brackets: dem Tisch (← der Tisch), der Kommode (← die Kommode), den Regalen (← die Regale, Pl.).

rules: Wo? is answered with the dative.
der → dem, das → dem, die → der, plural die → den (+ -n on the noun).
Typical verbs: stehen, sitzen, liegen, hängen.
The prepositions used here are auf, unter, an, neben, in, vor, hinter, über, zwischen.

vor / hinter der Kommode (← die Kommode)
über / zwischen den Regalen (← die Regale, Pl.)

topics.titleEn: Prepositions of place and their contractions
topics.summary: durch and um take the accusative; von, zu and bei the dative; in takes either.

explanation.heading: Always accusative
explanation.text: durch and um … (herum) take the accusative: durch den Park, um die Ecke herum.

explanation.heading: Always dative
explanation.text: von, zu and bei take the dative, and they contract with the article: von dem → vom, zu dem → zum, zu der → zur, bei dem → beim.

explanation.heading: From … to
explanation.text: A route is von … (bis) zu: vom Münster (bis) zum Bahnhof, von der Postgasse (bis) zur Kramgasse.

explanation.heading: in takes both
explanation.text: in answers wohin? with the accusative (in den Park, ins Haus) and wo? with the dative (im Bärenpark, in der Schweiz). in das → ins and in dem → im.

rules: durch, um … (herum): accusative.
von, zu, bei: dative.
Contractions: vom, zum, zur, beim, ins, im.
in + accusative answers wohin?; in + dative answers wo?
The feminine keeps its own forms: von der, zur, bei der, in die, in der.

examples.de: durch den Park / durch das Einkaufszentrum / durch die Stadt
examples.note: durch + accusative in all three genders

topics.titleEn: entlang, rein / raus, hin- and her-
topics.summary: More prepositions of place, plus the direction prefixes hin- (away) and her- (towards).

explanation.heading: Dative group
explanation.text: bei, (bis) zu and links / rechts / gegenüber von take the dative, and zu, bei and von contract with the article.

explanation.heading: entlang comes after
explanation.text: entlang takes the accusative and, unusually, is placed after the noun: Jörg soll die Kärntner Straße entlang gehen.

explanation.heading: The short forms
explanation.text: rein and raus are the short forms of hinein / herein and hinaus / heraus, especially common in spoken German. rein goes with in + accusative, raus with aus + dative.

explanation.heading: hin- or her-
explanation.text: her- means movement from a place towards the speaker (Komm heraus!); hin- means movement to a place away from the speaker (Jörg geht aus dem Museum hinaus).

rules: bei, (bis) zu, links / rechts / gegenüber von: dative.
Contractions: zu + dem = zum, zu + der = zur, bei + dem = beim, von + dem = vom.
entlang + accusative, placed after the noun.
rein = hinein / herein; raus = hinaus / heraus; both are colloquial short forms.
rein goes with in + accusative; raus goes with aus + dative.
her- = towards the speaker; hin- = away from the speaker.

topics.summary: Nine prepositions that take the accusative for movement and the dative for position.

explanation.heading: The nine
explanation.text: an, auf, in, über, unter, hinter, vor, neben, zwischen can take either case; the case is chosen by the question, not by the preposition.

explanation.heading: Wohin? → accusative
explanation.text: Movement towards a goal: Stell den Kaffee ins Regal! The contractions are an das → ans, auf das → aufs, in das → ins, and colloquially hinters, übers, unters, vors.

explanation.heading: Wo? → dative
explanation.text: Position: Der Kaffee steht im Regal. The contractions are an dem → am, in dem → im, and colloquially auf'm, hinterm, überm, unterm, vorm.

explanation.heading: A quick test
explanation.text: If the verb is stellen, legen, setzen, hängen (put) the case is accusative; with stehen, liegen, sitzen, hängen (be) it is dative.

rules: Wohin? → accusative. Wo? → dative.
Standard accusative contractions: ans, aufs, ins.
Standard dative contractions: am, im.
The document marks hinters, übers, unters, vors and auf'm, hinterm, überm, unterm, vorm as colloquial.
The same preposition can appear in both frames: ins Regal (wohin?) and im Regal (wo?).

examples.de: Stell den Kaffee ins Regal!
Der Kaffee steht im Regal.
an das → ans, auf das → aufs, in das → ins
an dem → am, in dem → im

exercises.prompt: Which contraction does the document mark as colloquial?

exercises.explain: The goal becomes a location, so the accusative ins becomes the dative im.

topics.summary: A preposition with the genitive, and an adverb that never starts the sentence.

explanation.heading: wegen + genitive
explanation.text: wegen names the reason as a noun phrase in the genitive: Wegen der Kombination aus Theorie und Praxis …

explanation.heading: nämlich is not a conjunction
explanation.text: nämlich is a connecting adverb. It stands inside the second sentence, after the conjugated verb — never in first position and never before it.

explanation.heading: What it does
explanation.text: The sentence with nämlich supplies the reason for the sentence before it: Ich muss ein Auslandssemester machen. Ich habe nämlich vor, …

rules: wegen takes the genitive and can open the sentence.
nämlich is a connecting adverb, placed after the conjugated verb in the middle field.
nämlich cannot stand in first position.
The nämlich sentence gives the reason for the statement before it.

examples.de: Wegen der Kombination aus Theorie und Praxis wäre ein Studium an einer FH sicher interessant.
Ich muss ein Auslandssemester machen. Ich habe nämlich vor, später für eine internationale Organisation zu arbeiten.

topics.titleEn: Counter-arguments: trotzdem, dennoch, zwar … aber, trotz
topics.summary: Four ways to concede a point and then argue against it.

explanation.heading: trotzdem and dennoch
explanation.text: Both are connectors standing at the front of the second sentence, so the verb follows immediately: Trotzdem ist das „Latinum“ heute nur noch selten Pflicht. dennoch is the more formal of the two.

explanation.heading: Where the conceded point sits
explanation.text: With trotzdem and dennoch the counter-argument is in the preceding main sentence; with zwar it is in the main clause itself, answered by aber.

explanation.heading: trotz + genitive
explanation.text: The preposition trotz packs the conceded point into a noun phrase: Trotz der Nützlichkeit von Lateinkenntnissen …

explanation.heading: A note on the zwar example
explanation.text: The document prints Zwar Lateinkenntnisse können …; in ordinary usage zwar follows the subject or the verb (Lateinkenntnisse können zwar …). The example is quoted here as printed.

rules: trotzdem and dennoch open the second sentence and are followed directly by the verb.
dennoch is more formal than trotzdem.
zwar … aber puts the conceded point and the objection in one sentence pair.
trotz takes the genitive.

examples.de: Lateinkenntnisse können im Studium sehr hilfreich sein. Trotzdem ist das „Latinum“ heute nur noch selten Pflicht.

topics.summary: Two main-clause connectors for a consequence, one everyday, one formal.

explanation.heading: What they do
explanation.text: In main clauses folglich or also express a result — the consequence of what was just said.

explanation.heading: Two positions
explanation.text: Both can stand at the beginning of the sentence or in the middle. At the beginning the verb follows immediately: Folglich ist man manchmal … In the middle the ordinary order is kept: Man ist folglich manchmal …

explanation.heading: Register
explanation.text: Sentences with folglich are more formal than sentences with also.

rules: also and folglich are main-clause connectors, not subordinating conjunctions.
In first position they are followed directly by the conjugated verb.
In the middle field they stand after the conjugated verb.
folglich is more formal than also.

explanation.heading: Two cases, two registers
explanation.text: Alternatives can be expressed using statt + genitive in standard usage, or statt + dative colloquially: Statt der Grünen / Statt den Grünen.

explanation.heading: statt before a preposition
explanation.text: statt is also used with prepositions. Then it simply stands in front of the whole prepositional phrase and does not govern a case of its own: Statt im Mai, Statt für die SPD.

explanation.heading: Position
explanation.text: In both examples the statt phrase opens the sentence, so the conjugated verb follows in second position: … wählt Lisa …, … war die Wahl …

rules: statt + genitive is the standard form; statt + dative is colloquial.
statt can also stand in front of a prepositional phrase, which keeps its own case.
A statt phrase in first position is followed by the conjugated verb.

topics.summary: A preposition naming the time during which something happens.

explanation.heading: What it says
explanation.text: The preposition während expresses a time in which something happens — during, in the course of.

explanation.heading: Two cases
explanation.text: The standard case is the genitive: während seines Besuchs. Colloquially the dative is heard: während seinem Besuch.

explanation.heading: Not the same as the conjunction
explanation.text: This während is a preposition and takes a noun phrase. The conjunction während, which introduces a whole clause with a verb at the end, is a different word.

rules: während + genitive is standard; während + dative is colloquial.
It names the period during which something happens.
It is followed by a noun phrase, not a clause.
